clue.text: One could be attracted to fly paper?

definitions.text: One could be attracted to fly paper?

parts.words: One could be attracted to fly paper
parts.note: read the clue as an insect that might get stuck on sticky fly paper, and also as a creature whose name begins with the word for adhering

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of creature ends up caught on a sticky fly trap.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly paper is a sticky strip that traps insects; the answer is a twig-like insect whose name starts with the very thing such paper does.
explanation.definitionFit: A phasmid that mimics a twig is an insect, and any insect could be caught on sticky fly paper.

clue.text: Paid to be comfortable

explanation.surface: Someone who has been paid now feels at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that has been paid is settled, and a person at home and at ease in a place is settled there.

clue.text: I would have one before returning to that half-wit!

indicators.note: before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the next one in the answer

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: returning means the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker, about to go back to a fool, says they would rather have one first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is only a link; the exclamation suggests someone heading back to a fool, but 'returning' applies only to the little word next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-wit is a foolish, stupid person, a synonym.

clue.text: A time in Kentucky was enough, grasshopper

indicators.note: in places the letters for a time inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky
was enough means did, as in 'that did' = that sufficed

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a spell in Kentucky that was plenty for them, addressing a grasshopper.
explanation.walkthrough: A katydid is a North American bush cricket, a kind of long-horned grasshopper.
explanation.definitionFit: The katydid is a green North American insect of the long-horned grasshopper family.

clue.text: Observed how the drinks may be served

definitions.text: how the drinks may be served

explanation.surface: A remark on watching how drinks are served at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words: drinks served without ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Observed means spotted or seen; the second sense reads the letters as NOT ICED, a way to serve a drink without cubes.

clue.text: Pen half then finish

parts.note: in printing an en is a unit of width half of an em
finish means closure, the end of something

explanation.surface: A writer's note to complete half a job and then stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is the noun for an animal fold; 'half' is the printers' en, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen for animals is a fenced area, which is an enclosure.

clue.text: Some digital coverage

parts.note: digital is read as relating to digits, fingers and toes, and coverage as a horny plate over one

explanation.surface: Some reporting carried online or on electronic media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computers, but here it means to do with digits, the fingers and toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nail covers the tip of a digit of the foot, so it is part of the covering on digits.

clue.text: Dispatch note?

parts.note: dispatch read as kill, and note as a written list of names

explanation.surface: A delivery slip sent with a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: A dispatch note usually goes with goods; here 'dispatch' means do away with, and the note lists targets.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster of people marked for killing or removal is a written list of those to be dispatched.

clue.text: One employed to put locks on bedroom furniture?

definitions.text: One employed to put locks on bedroom furniture?

parts.words: One employed to put locks on bedroom furniture
parts.note: locks read as tresses of hair, and bedroom furniture as a chest of drawers, which stack into the job title

explanation.surface: A locksmith hired to fit locks to wardrobes and chests in a bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks are HAIR and a piece of bedroom furniture is a DRESSER; together they name the worker who styles hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist employed in a salon cuts and arranges customers' hair for a living.

clue.text: Beaters find the queen covered in insects

indicators.note: covered in says the royal abbreviation is wrapped by the word for the bloodsucking insects

parts.note: ticks are small bloodsucking parasites, loosely called insects
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Gamekeepers' beaters come upon the monarch crawling with bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaters' suggests the shoot's beaters; it means hearts, which tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is slang for the heart, the organ that beats.

clue.text: Theresa west married her lovers

indicators.note: married signals the two names are joined and their letters combined into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Theresa West wed the men who loved her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'married' is the anagram signal for THERESA WEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweethearts are people in love, a synonym for lovers.

clue.text: Permit given to popular stretch of water

indicators.note: given to says the word for permit is attached after the word for popular

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A licence issued for a well-liked body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea or a lake reaching inland, a stretch of water.

clue.text: Degree given to redcoat — for dancing!

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A qualification is awarded to a holiday-camp entertainer for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcoat is an entertainer at a British holiday camp. 'dancing' rearranges TO and REDCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest university degree, such as a PhD.

clue.text: Worked out leaders of Durham university council were in action

indicators.note: in puts the picked letters inside the word for an action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: leaders of takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Senior figures at a Durham university council were seen to be busy at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is an English university city. 'leaders of' gives DUC, set 'in' DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have deduced something is to have reasoned it out from evidence.

clue.text: Deterioration in organization runs and runs, thus no-one comes back

parts.note: CO, company, is a business organisation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: comes back says each of the last two pieces is read backwards in place

parts.note: so means thus
NO and I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A company's decline as it keeps running on and nobody returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns SO into OS and NOI into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrosion is a gradual wearing away or decay, a form of deterioration.

clue.text: Uncertainty surrounding the French old-fashioned garb

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for uncertainty is wrapped round the French article

parts.note: doubt is uncertainty
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Doubt hangs over the French in their dated clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting man's jacket worn in Renaissance times, a period garment.

clue.text: Mope around — then breeze back to the shops

indicators.note: around signals the letters of mope are moved about
back says the word for a breeze is read the other way

parts.note: air is a light breeze

explanation.surface: Someone sulks for a while, then drifts back to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link before the definition; 'around' sounds like loitering but signals the anagram, and 'back' applies only to the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, plural of emporium, are large stores or marketplaces.

clue.text: Short film about the ultimate material

indicators.note: about says the short film is placed around the word for ultimate

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
ultimate means final or last

explanation.surface: A brief movie about the finest fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short film' is not a short but PIC, the shortened word for a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is a synthetic substance moulded into countless goods, a material.

clue.text: Hail storm that's about normal

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, a hail
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: A hailstorm described as roughly what one would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail storm' looks like weather; it is a greeting and a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical or ordinary, a synonym for normal.

clue.text: Accept there's quiet and carry on

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to resume is to carry on after a pause

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that silence is called for and continues.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to take something as true without proof, to accept it.

clue.text: Pressure on resistance — a queue for confection

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
a line is a queue of people

explanation.surface: Pushy people force their way through a queue for sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Praline is a sweet made of nuts in boiled sugar, a confection.

clue.text: A sudden increase in desire to chase drug highs

indicators.note: to chase puts the word for desire behind the drug highs, following them

parts.note: ups, or uppers, are stimulant highs
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A rise in the craving to pursue a narcotic buzz.
explanation.definitionFit: An upsurge is a sharp rise, a sudden increase.

clue.text: Clean up a theatrical performance for serialisation

parts.note: to soap is to wash, clean up
an opera is a staged musical drama

explanation.surface: A theatre production is spruced up before being broadcast in episodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running broadcast drama told in episodes is a serial, an example of serialisation.

clue.text: Might one endure endless unhappiness?

indicators.note: endless means the word for unhappiness loses its last letter

parts.note: misery is great unhappiness

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone could put up with ceaseless sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a hoarder lives meanly, putting up with unhappiness, and 'endless' cuts MISERY short.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad who hoards money lives frugally and miserably, enduring wretchedness.

clue.text: Raising target admits an obsession

indicators.note: admits says the turned word lets the other piece inside it
raising in a down clue means the word for target is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an aim is a target

explanation.surface: Lifting a goal reveals an obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns AIM to MIA, which 'admits' AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mania is an extreme enthusiasm or compulsive craze, an obsession.

clue.text: Brian is terrible — sending back drink!

annotationWithheld.why: Brian is terrible - sending back drink! (7): RETSINA is ANISTER hidden in 'Brian is terrible' reversed, but no clue word signals the hidden word; 'sending back' would have to signal both the hiding and the reversal, a word doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Brian is terrible — sending back drink!

clue.text: Organs finding a way into hostelries

indicators.note: into places the a and the way inside the word for hostelries

parts.note: inns are hostelries
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Musical organs turn up on a road going into pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Innards are the internal organs of the body, the guts.

clue.text: American soldier, freed, at once became confused

indicators.note: became confused signals that the letters of the words get mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A US soldier, released from captivity, was instantly bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became confused' rearranges FREED and AT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Confederate was a soldier of the southern states in the American Civil War.
